video_title: Full Denver Nuggets Postgame Media Availability vs. CHI 🎙

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on team conditioning and transition defense issues
quotes.excerpt: Our transition defense was embarrassing until the fourth quarter. I thought the young guys were pretty good.
quotes.quote: They needed conditioning because they didn't get in the first half, they didn't get back. Our transition defense was embarrassing until the fourth quarter. I thought the young guys were pretty good. And obviously that's going to hurt us, and teams like that have hurt us over the years, not just tonight, but in the past years. Younger teams that play fast, advance the ball, and look for advantages, and two-on-ones, and three-on-twos, and it'll be good film for them to watch.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman says the Nuggets transition defense was embarrassing until the fourth quarter and admits it is an area that has hurt the team in past years.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Bryce Hopkins' growing confidence and athleticism
quotes.excerpt: I'd say the confidence to explode more consistently. I've seen it more and more.
quotes.quote: I'd say the confidence to explode more consistently. I think there's times, I thought last year Bryce felt like he was trying to protect himself in situations that he didn't want to, you'd rather use his body than use his athleticism to jump and go get the ball. But I've seen it more and more, there's more confidence to go do that. Again, I'm not a doctor, but it seems like he feels good. And it was good to see him make that third quarter run confidently, not just because he was making shots, I just thought he played with some good pace in the third quarter.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman is seeing more confidence from Bryce Hopkins this preseason saying he is finally using his athleticism to go get the ball instead of trying to protect himself.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Bryce Hopkins' ability to play to his strengths
quotes.excerpt: What I'm realizing about Bryce is he plays to his strengths. And the guys that can figure that out early, usually survive.
quotes.quote: Bryce is really good. What I'm realizing about Bryce is he plays to his strengths. And the guys that can figure that out early, usually survive. Long way to go, but just his ability to attack the basket, use his body, crash the offensive glass, that's one thing we did well. We had 20 second-chance points and could have had a lot more. We missed out on nine opportunities when we got the ball back. But Bryce, he has some special skills, and he has things he has to work on, and I think that's one of these guys that's very comfortable with that. His process will be better if he stays in his lane, and that's what he did tonight.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on Bryce Hopkins: The guys that can figure out how to play to their strengths early usually survive in this league.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Jamal Murray's play and officiating
quotes.excerpt: I saw the replay late. I should have challenged that because the initial contact was I thought a foul.
quotes.quote: I saw the replay late. I should have challenged that because the initial contact was I thought a foul, and then he reacted to that contact. So I was very surprised that wasn't a foul. It was very similar to the alpha foul with Giddy, where they're kind of 50/50, but the offensive player has obviously wins that battle with the officials. But no, he's been okay. Jamal, it just kind of reminds me of last year. He has a really good way about him right now. Made some unbelievable passes again. I just think it's because he plays with Jokic, you just take it for granted, man. The pocket passes this guy throws, the simplicity of how he plays, it was good to see. He had the five assists.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on Jamal Murray: He has a really good way about him right now and is making some unbelievable passes.

quotes.speaker: Bryce Hopkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Bryce Hopkins on his comfort level in training camp
quotes.excerpt: I'd probably say about an eight. I feel already more comfortable out there now.
quotes.quote: I'd probably say about an eight. I feel already more comfortable out there now. Just it was a blessing just being out there, playing in front of the crowd tonight, being on the home court. Fans pretty much came out here and showed us a lot of support for the first preseason game, so it was definitely a blessing to be out there.
quotes.social_post: Bryce Hopkins says he feels much more comfortable heading into his first preseason game with the Nuggets.

quotes.speaker: Bryce Hopkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Bryce Hopkins on learning his role and positional versatility
quotes.excerpt: Big thing for me is I can play different positions, so being able to know the two-spot, three-spot, and four-spot is going to be big for me.
quotes.quote: I feel like the biggest thing is just when we're out there in practice, it's just making sure I'm watching the guys in front of me, making sure I know exactly what I'm doing when I get out there and it's my turn. But you know, a big thing for me is I can play different positions, so being able to know the two-spot, three-spot, and four-spot is going to be big for me. So just being in practice and when we're scripting our plays, I'm just trying to be locked in on that part.
quotes.social_post: Bryce Hopkins says his goal is to master multiple positions for the Nuggets this season: I can play the two, three, and four spot.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on learning the team's system and options
quotes.excerpt: A lot of options is what it's like. We've formally put in probably a smaller percentage of the totality of what we run.
quotes.quote: A lot of options is what it's like. We've formally put in probably a smaller percentage of the totality of what we run. But it's just being able to have counters and being able to take advantage of what we see on the court. We've been putting in a new player, or remembering a new player too, every day or so. And just with this group, it's just it's a lot to guard.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson on the Nuggets offense: We have a lot of options and counters to take advantage of what we see on the court.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on learning Jokic's role and slowing down the game
quotes.excerpt: Getting a better feel for Jokic's role and where he is in the pocket and where our shake-up guys are.
quotes.quote: Getting a better feel for Jokic's role and where he is in the pocket and where our shake-up guys are. And you know, we usually have a guy in the dunker. So just getting a feel for that. It's just reps and comfortability, and I'm it's slowing down. I think that's the main thing. It slowed down at one point last year where, you know, something I've been doing for so long, but last year for some reason, the beginning of the season, it just felt so fast. So to slow it down is helpful and makes me feel like I can see and read and play off of that.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson says the game is slowing down for him this year: It felt so fast at the beginning of last season but now I feel like I can see and read the game.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on the impact of having Aaron Gordon on the floor
quotes.excerpt: He's a problem. He's a problem and he's just playing with confidence, shooting the ball well, attacking.
quotes.quote: He's a problem. He's a problem and he's just playing with confidence, shooting the ball well, attacking. You know, he adds a lot of dimensions that it's unique in a sense, how he's kind of able to dominate certain aspects of the game and you can see how much it stresses the other teams out. So to see him running around, looking healthy and playing hard is huge for us.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson on Aaron Gordon: He is a problem and he adds a lot of dimensions that are unique. It is huge to see him running around looking healthy and playing hard.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on team offensive efficiency and shot selection
quotes.excerpt: My goal is for us to just have a fluid and efficient offense as we can.
quotes.quote: My goal is for us to just have a fluid and efficient offense as we can. And I think last year it's not about make, it's not about attempts, it's about getting the looks that we generate well as a team. So I think it's the same thing. Maybe that volume goes up and there's there's definitely an aspect of hunting down a couple more. But I don't get too caught up on the number. I think last year is an example of that. I don't get too caught up on how many I shoot, I just try to make the ones that I do shoot and try to and try to hunt the quality ones and try to make our offense as efficient as possible.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson on his offensive role: I do not get too caught up on the number of shots I take, I just try to hunt the quality ones and make our offense as efficient as possible.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on spacing and defensive coverage
quotes.excerpt: I think I got stuck a lot last year where I'd be on the wing or in the corner and I'd feel like I'm pulling my man out of the play.
quotes.quote: I think I got stuck a lot last year where I'd be on the wing or in the corner and I'd feel like I'm pulling my man out of the play. It feels like it's maybe even four-on-four where like that guy's not going to like go ahead and please help. Like I'll tell it to go ahead, please help, and I'll get a shot. But if it doesn't, then you end up staying in the corner, you get a little bit removed from the game. So last year, after I found ways to get myself in actions in the flow of our offense, I think is when you start feeling like a basketball player again and that's when things start happening, and a lot of times those are positive.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson on finding his rhythm: After I found ways to get myself in actions in the flow of our offense, that is when you start feeling like a basketball player again.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on mentoring Bryce Hopkins
quotes.excerpt: Bryce is a really talented player, and he, you know, he showed his stuff tonight.
quotes.quote: Bryce is a really talented player, and he, you know, he showed his stuff tonight and he's been showing his stuff throughout all of camp. A lot of the ways you can get on the court as a young guy in the NBA is just by doing the little simple things: running the court, getting to the corner, proper spacing, proper defensive coverages and like if the coaches trust you, that gives you a lot of opportunity to be on the court. So on that shot, I'm like when you have somebody that's kind of is a kind of like a wild three, if you close out too wild then you're going to foul him. I just told him like, hey, make sure you close out to the side of him. Go ahead, jump, attack the shooter, but you got like I've done it plenty of times myself. You want to get to the side of him because if he has a leg kick or jumps a little higher than you thought and your body like they're they're going to call it and it's it's a big thing in today's game. You will get called for that, more so than college. College, they're less likely to call fouls on threes for whatever reason. But he's very receptive. All the young guys we have on the team are very receptive.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson is mentoring rookie Bryce Hopkins on defensive discipline: I told him to make sure you close out to the side of the shooter to avoid those fouls.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on his connection to Caleb and Carolina
quotes.excerpt: I like to play in that. A Carolina has an alumni game every summer.
quotes.quote: I like to play in that. A Carolina has an alumni game every summer. And I like to go back because when I was a player, it was really cool seeing the NBA guys come and play in front of the campers. It's in front of kids' campers. And so I try to make a point to get back there and play with my old teammates and stuff and you know, just spend some time with the guys that are there. So this was two summers ago that I was playing. And a lot of the times the freshmen will be put with the veterans, right? So Caleb was on my team. And I knew him, I knew he was a highly touted guy, I knew, you know, he was he was a really good prospect, but I didn't know how ready he was till I got in that game. Like this dude's a freak. Dunking stuff, and then he's like you can see him starting to figure out the game. So I paid attention to Caleb, you know, all throughout that season and you know, I was high on him from day one. I'm like he's kind of like, you know, he's kind of playing down a little bit in terms of like he's not playing as much of a four as he was, but he reminded me of like a a younger, smaller Kevin Garnett, like a 2026 Kevin Garnett. Just talented, can athletically gifted, and so he has a really bright future ahead of him.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson recalls playing with Caleb at a Carolina alumni game: I knew he was a highly touted guy, but I did not know how ready he was until I got in that game. This dude is a freak.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson on improving transition defense
quotes.excerpt: It is a bit of an oversimplification to an extent. There's things that we're trying to do.
quotes.quote: It is a bit of an oversimplification to an extent. There's things that we're trying to do to make it, to make ourselves better at it. You can obviously just sprint back, but there's a balance, you know. We like to attack the paint. We like to attack the paint, we like to get shooters flat in the corners, or to get people flat on baselines, so that's like full sprints back and forth. So we have some things that we're working on to kind of shore up that area of the game. But it's definitely I mean I, you know, it's definitely something we need to get better at. So it's just something we're focusing on and we take the tape, we watch the tape, see where we went wrong, and so we'll build it, you know, we will build it. It's not something that we're going to say, oh, we'll do it when regular season comes. No, we're we're going to find ways to right now, right here, right now, find ways to improve upon that. And some of it is the simple simple like just get back and some of it is um maybe a little bit more slightly schematic.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson admits the Nuggets need to improve their transition defense: It is something we are focusing on and we will find ways to improve right here, right now.
